checked.comment: Matches Section 3. Rewards are in [0,1] with E[r|x] = x^T theta*, ||x|| <= 1 and ||theta*|| <= 1. An oblivious adversary chooses the K context vectors, and rewards are independent given the contexts. Mapping this to stochastic_iid noise with adversarial_contexts and an oblivious_sequence is reasonable. learner_knows {T, K, d} covers the SupLinUCB inputs (T, and alpha depends on T and K).

Theorem 1: with alpha = sqrt(1/2 ln(2TK/delta)), the regret is O(sqrt(T d ln^3(KT ln(T)/delta))) with probability at least 1-delta. The paper defines regret on realised rewards against a*_t. The expression, tuning, high-probability type and known horizon all match.

Theorem 2: E[sum_t max_a x_{t,a}^T theta* - sum_t r_{t,a_t}] >= gamma sqrt(Td) for any algorithm, with T >= K >= 2 and d^2 <= T. This is pseudo-regret against the per-round best action; side, conditions and expression all match.

summary: The extraction is accurate. Theorem 1 (the high-probability upper bound for SupLinUCB) and Theorem 2 (the Omega(sqrt(Td)) lower bound) are both recorded correctly, and the single setting is mapped sensibly onto the controlled vocabulary. The remaining lemmas are technical and correctly left out, the cited results match the text, and no corrections are needed.
